title: Gaffrey Lab Infant Microstates and Attention
description: This dataset comprises high-density EEG recordings from 43 infants aged 5-10 months, collected as part of a broader study on the impact of bias and discrimination on maternal and infant health outcomes. Infants viewed relaxing videos while EEG was recorded to examine microstates and attention-related neural dynamics during early development. The data were collected at Duke University with appropriate ethical oversight and informed caregiver consent.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz referenced to the vertex (Cz) using a 128-channel HydroCel Geodesic Sensor Net (Electrical Geodesics, Eugene, OR), with impedances kept below 50 kilohms. Infants sat on their caregiver's lap and watched up to 15 minutes of relaxing videos with sound (10, 90-second videos separated by breaks), presented via E-Prime software, preceded by a three-second attention-grabbing video clip.
